hypotheses.justification: The proof uses `hlen` only in `have hi' : i < next.length := by omega`, to turn `hi : i < (C.stepOfL Δ).length` into `i < next.length`. That bound follows from `hlab` and `hx`. Take `hlab i hi : C.Q.labelAt (x ++ [i]) = some _`. `QuasiTab.labelAt q x` is `(q.atOpt x).map label`. `QuasiTab.atOpt_snoc` gives `q.atOpt (x ++ [i]) = (q.atOpt x).bind (fun n => n.children[i]?)`. With `hx` and `children (QNode k Δ next) = next` (rfl), the label is `(next[i]?).map label`. It equals `some _`, so `next[i]?` is some, hence `i < next.length`. In Lean: `rw [QuasiTab.labelAt, QuasiTab.atOpt_snoc, hx] at h` and a simp using `List.getElem?_eq_none` / isSome. The rest of the proof only needs `hi'` and is unchanged. Degenerate case `next = []`: the same argument shows `stepOfL Δ` is empty, so `nonBasicStep` yields no index and nothing changes.
